summary: Unexpected 5xx surge following runtime hotpatch triggering connection-reset loop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses from API endpoints after we deployed a runtime hotpatch to the us-east serving fleet. The surge manifested as a short-lived but high-rate wave of 502/503 responses and streaming disconnects for multiple tenants, most prominently NimbleDocs (enterprise).

Impact:
- NimbleDocs observed ~18% error rate on generation endpoints for ~12 minutes (03:12-03:24 UTC).
- User-facing failures for both sync and streaming calls.
- Some requests experienced long tail retries from SDK clients.

Environment:
- Prod: us-east serving fleet (hotpatch rollout started 2026-03-13 03:05 UTC)
- Affected services: api-gateway proxy, connection-proxy (sidecar), serving-runtime v2.4.7+hotfix

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Trigger a medium burst of prompts against customer tenant (scale test from CS).
2) Runtime instance that received hotpatch restarted and rejoined; during warmup connection-proxy returned RST to upstream.
3) Api-gateway retried to multiple upstreams, amplifying connection churn and causing backlog in the runtime accept queue.
4) Backpressure resulted in synchronous 502/503 responses and streaming session resets.

Logs / Evidence:
- Sample api-gateway logs: repeated "upstream connection reset" and 502/503 spikes aligned with restart window. (link: logs: #slack-logs channel / bound to INC-2026-0313-07)
- Serving-runtime logs show repeated prefetch eviction warnings and "kv-cache reinit" messages immediately after hotpatch.
- Dynatrace traces show acceptance latency spike and connection pool saturation at the proxy layer.

Notes:
- Hotpatch targeted a kernel fallback mitigation in v2.4.7 and was rolled with a 10% initial batch. Symptoms appeared during the canary ramp to 30%.
comments: 2026-03-13 03:20 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Received NimbleDocs alert. Notified oncall SRE and escalated to Engineering. Collected request IDs and sample traces.

2026-03-13 03:33 UTC - Diego Martinez (SRE): Observed restart/rejoin pattern on 6 runtime pods that received hotpatch. Opening hypothesis that connection-proxy didn't drain accept queue before restart.

2026-03-13 04:05 UTC - Priya Verma (Runtime Eng): Confirmed new binary includes a change to accept backlog handling. Reproduced connection-reset locally with patched binary + proxy offset. Creating PR to add graceful drain and increase accept backlog. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
2026-03-13 05:12 UTC - CS Rep (J. Adler): Customer acknowledged reduced errors after rollback and requested timeline and a postmortem.
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - Diego Martinez (SRE): Rolling postmortem draft assigned; added follow-ups for better hotpatch rollout gating and synthetic smoke test before batch increase.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses evaluated:
- H1: Hotpatch binary caused accept queue reset behavior that combined with proxy retries produced amplified connection churn. Evidence: commit changed accept backlog handling and runtime logs show immediate kv-cache reinit and eviction cycles.
- H2: API gateway retry settings + canary ramp percentage created retry storm. Evidence: traces show retries fan-out to multiple upstreams during restart window.
- H3: Autoscaler reacted to errors and triggered new pods causing further churn. Evidence: autoscaler activity correlates but appears secondary.

Actions taken:
- Immediate rollback of hotpatch in us-east at 03:28 UTC; error rate returned to baseline by 03:36 UTC.
- Increased protection on api-gateway for endpoints serving enterprise tenants: lowered retry fanout to 1 during transient upstream failures and enabled short 2s backoff.
- Disabled auto-ramp beyond 10% canary for this patch class until fix is merged.
- Gathered logs and traces and linked PR to this ticket.

Relevant links:
- Trace center: https://app.datadog.com/trace/INC-2026-0313-07
- Slack thread: #inc-2026-0313-hotpatch (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345)
resolution:
Mitigation and next steps:
1) Rollback completed (03:28 UTC) returned error rates to baseline; customer incident acknowledged as resolved.
2) Engineering produced PR to add graceful accept-queue drain and delay proxy reconnects on restart (PR merged 2026-03-14).
3) Deployments: fixed runtime version will be rolled with stricter canary gating and an automated smoke test to exercise connection-proxy interactions prior to ramp.
4) Postmortem and runbook updates: add a preflight smoke check and a throttled backoff policy for api-gateway retries during runtime restarts.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Diego Martinez: verify rollout plan and synthetic smoke tests (due 2026-03-18).
- Priya Verma: monitor canary metrics and validate fixes in staging (due 2026-03-16).
- CS: provide customer timeline and RCA (Aisha Patel to draft).
